name: God's Character
wording: God is one: Father, Son and Holy Spirit are the one Yahweh (Deut 6:4; Matt 28:19; 1 Cor 8:6).

- John 1:1–3; 8:58; Col 1:16–17: he is God, was before all things, and all was made through him.
- Phil 2:9–11: he is given the name above every name; every tongue confesses him Lord.
- John 1:14, 18; 14:9; Col 1:15; Heb 1:3: whoever has seen him has seen the Father.
- Matt 1:21, 23: Yeshua, Yahweh saves; Immanuel, God with us.
- Mark 1:40–42; Matt 9:10–13; 12:20; Luke 4:18: he touches the unclean, eats with sinners, frees the oppressed and does not break a bruised reed.
- John 10:11, 18: the good shepherd who lays down his life of his own accord.
- Heb 2:14–18; 4:15: truly human, tempted without sin, merciful and faithful.
- Rom 5:12–21; 1 Cor 15:22, 45: the last Adam; over against Adam, humanity, he is the righteous human.
- 1 Tim 2:6; Heb 2:9; 2 Cor 5:14–15: he suffered and died for all.
- Acts 17:31; Matt 25:31–32: the one who died for people will judge them.
Jesus is Yahweh with us, truly God and truly human: all that God is finds full expression in his human life. He stands for humanity as the righteous human, and he suffered and died for all.

- Matt 28:19; 1 Cor 2:10–11: he shares the one name and knows the depths of God.
- Gen 1:2; Ps 139:7: he is there from creation, and where he is, God is.
- Job 33:4; Ps 104:29–30; Ezek 37:14; Rom 8:11: he gives life and raises the dead.
- Isa 63:10; Eph 4:30; 1 Cor 12:11: he is personal, wills, and can be grieved.
- John 14:16–17, 26; 15:26; Rom 8:26–27: the Advocate who teaches, testifies to Jesus and prays for us.
- Rom 8:2; Ezek 36:26–27: he sets free and renews the heart.
- 2 Cor 3:18; Gal 5:22–23: he makes people like Christ; his fruit includes love, patience, goodness and faithfulness.

The Spirit is Yahweh's own living presence and power, fully God and personal, not a go-between. He draws near, gives life, speaks truth, helps, sets free and makes people holy. What he brings about in people shows who God is.

- 1 John 4:8, 16: God is love.
- John 17:24: the Father loved the Son before the world existed.
- John 3:16; Rom 5:8: he gave his Son; Christ died for us while we were still sinners.
- Isa 49:15; 66:13; Matt 23:37; Deut 32:11: he comforts like a mother and protects like an eagle over its young.
- John 15:13; Rom 5:5: the Son lays down his life; the Spirit pours God's love into hearts.
- Heb 12:6: he disciplines those he loves.

Love is who God is, within his own eternal life and toward all he has made. He seeks the good of those he loves at cost to himself, and protects them fiercely. His discipline and his anger serve that love: his wrath is never arbitrary, but opposes what corrupts and destroys.

- Ps 119:68: he is good and does what is good.
- Ps 145:9: Yahweh is good to all.
- 1 John 1:5: God is light, with no darkness in him.
- James 1:13, 17: he tempts no one to evil; every good gift comes from him.
- Gen 1:31: all he made was very good.
- John 10:11; Acts 10:38: Jesus is the good shepherd who went about doing good.
- Neh 9:20: his Spirit is called good.
- Isa 5:20: woe to those who call evil good.
God is good and does good. There is no evil in him, and he leads no one into it.

- Gen 18:25: the Judge of all the earth does what is right.
- Deut 32:4; Ps 89:14: all his ways are just; justice carries his throne.
- Exod 34:7: he does not leave guilt unpunished, and its consequences reach later generations.
- Ezek 18:20; Deut 24:16: a child does not bear the guilt of a parent; each answers for their own sin.
- Rom 2:6, 11: he repays each according to their deeds, without favouritism.
- Luke 12:47–48: the penalty matches what a person knew and did.
- Deut 10:17–18; Ps 103:6; Lev 19:15: he takes up the cause of the wronged and demands fair judgment.
- Rom 3:25–26: at the cross he shows that he is just.
- Acts 3:14; John 5:30; 16:8: Jesus is the Righteous One whose judgment is just; the Spirit exposes sin and shows what is right.

God judges truthfully, fairly and in due measure, never arbitrarily. He does not call the guilty innocent. Each person answers for their own deeds: no one is held guilty for what another did, although the consequences of sin can reach others. His justice defends the wronged.
## God is compassionate, gracious and forgiving

- Exod 34:6–7: his own words about himself: compassionate, gracious, forgiving, yet not ignoring guilt.
- Jer 31:20: his heart yearns for Ephraim as for a child.
- Ps 103:8–13; Mic 7:18–19; Isa 43:25: he removes sin and delights in mercy.
- Luke 15:20: the father runs to meet his returning son.
- Isa 53:4–6: the guilt of all is laid on the servant.
- Matt 9:36; Heb 4:15; Rom 8:26: Jesus is moved by the crowds and shares our weakness; the Spirit helps in it.

God is moved by the need of people as a parent by a child. His grace gives what no one has earned. He forgives truly and gladly, yet not cheaply: he does not pretend guilt is nothing, but bears its cost himself.

- Exod 34:6; Num 14:18; Nah 1:3: slow to anger, and not leaving guilt unpunished.
- Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2: because he is slow to anger, people may return, and he relents.
- Gen 15:16: he waits generations before judging the Amorites.
- Rom 2:4; 3:25; 2 Pet 3:9: his patience gives room to turn; he does not want anyone to perish.
- 1 Tim 1:16; Gal 5:22: Christ shows perfect patience; the Spirit brings forth patience in people.
God is slow to anger and gives time to change, so there is room for mercy. His patience is not indifference to evil. It has an end, because he does not leave guilt and wrong standing for ever.

- Exod 34:6; Deut 7:9; Mic 7:20: abounding in covenant love, keeping what he swore.
- Mal 3:6: because he does not change, the descendants of Jacob are not destroyed.
- Gen 9:8–17; 15:17: he binds himself by promise, and alone passes between the pieces.
- Lam 3:22–23: his compassion is new every morning, even in ruin.
- 2 Tim 2:13: he remains faithful when people are not.
- Matt 4:1–11; Heb 2:17: Jesus is faithful where Israel failed, a faithful high priest.
- 2 Cor 1:20; Rev 19:11; Eph 1:13–14: his promises find their yes in Christ, called Faithful and True; the Spirit is their guarantee.
God's love is loyal and active: he does what he has committed himself to, even when people fail. He does not act against his own character.
## God is jealous in his love

- Exod 20:5–6; 34:14; Deut 4:24: he is a jealous God who will not share his people with other gods.
- Isa 54:5; Hos 2:19–20: he binds himself to them as a husband, for ever.
- Joel 2:18; Zech 8:2–3; Isa 9:7: his zeal spares, restores and brings about justice and peace.
- John 2:17: zeal for the Father's house consumes Jesus.

God's love is not indifferent. He wants the whole heart of those he loves, because what takes his place harms them. His jealousy is not envy or insecurity: it is the zeal of faithful love that defends and restores.

- Isa 6:3–7: holy, holy, holy; he cleanses the man who is undone before him.
- Exod 3:5; Lev 10:1–3: his presence is not to be treated lightly.
- Lev 16:30; Heb 10:19–22: he himself provides the way to be cleansed and come near.
- Lev 19:2: his people are to be holy as he is.
- Hos 11:8–9: as the Holy One among his people, he holds back his anger.
- Mark 1:24; Heb 7:26: Jesus is the Holy One of God, without stain.
- Ps 51:11; 1 Cor 6:19; 2 Cor 3:18: the Holy Spirit lives in people and changes them.

God is wholly himself, morally pure and beyond comparison. Evil cannot stand unchanged before him, yet he provides the way to come near and makes people holy. His holiness and his love belong together.

- Exod 34:6: abounding in faithfulness and truth.
- Num 23:19; Titus 1:2; Heb 6:18: he does not and cannot lie.
- John 12:49–50; 14:6; 17:17: Jesus speaks what the Father gave him; he is the truth.
- John 16:13; 1 John 5:6: the Spirit is the truth and leads into it.
God does not deceive. What he reveals about himself is how he really is, so he can be trusted.

- Job 12:13; Rom 16:27: wisdom belongs to him; he alone is wise.
- Prov 3:19; 8:22–31; Ps 104:24; Jer 10:12: he made the world by wisdom.
- Job 28:23–28; Prov 9:10: he knows the way to wisdom; for people it begins with the fear of Yahweh.
- Eccl 3:11; 8:17; Isa 55:8–9; Rom 11:33: people cannot fathom all he does.
- James 1:5; 3:17: he gives wisdom generously; it is pure, peace-loving, gentle and full of mercy.
- Luke 2:52; Matt 12:42; 1 Cor 1:23–25, 30; Col 2:3: Jesus grew in wisdom, is greater than Solomon, and the crucified Christ is the wisdom of God.
- Isa 11:2; Eph 1:17: the Spirit is the Spirit of wisdom.

God sees the whole and knows how to bring about what is good. His wisdom orders creation, goes beyond human understanding and can be trusted where people cannot see why. For people wisdom begins with revering him, and he gives it generously to those who ask. It is seen most fully in the crucified Christ.

- Gen 17:1; Rev 1:8: he is God Almighty.
- Gen 18:14; Job 42:2; Jer 32:17, 27; Matt 19:26: nothing is too difficult for him, and no purpose of his can be thwarted.
- Luke 1:35, 37: no word of his will fail.
- Mark 4:39–41; Matt 28:18: wind and sea obey Jesus; all authority is given to him.
- Zech 4:6; Eph 1:19–20: he works by his Spirit, and his power raised Christ from the dead.
- 1 Cor 1:24–25; 2 Cor 12:9: his power is shown in the crucified Christ and perfected in weakness.
Nothing God purposes is beyond him. His power creates, saves and raises the dead. It always serves who he is, and it is seen most strikingly in the weakness of the cross.

- Gen 3:8–9: he comes looking for those who hide.
- Exod 3:12; 25:8; 33:14: he goes with his people and wants to dwell among them.
- Ps 139:7: there is no place away from his presence.
- Matt 1:23: Immanuel, God with us.
- John 14:23; 1 Cor 3:16: he makes his home with people by his Spirit.
- Rev 21:3: God himself will dwell with them.
God takes the first step toward people and desires to live among them: in the tabernacle, in Jesus, by his Spirit, and finally in a renewed creation.

- Gen 1:31: all he made was very good.
- Gen 2:7; Job 33:4: his breath gives life.
- Ps 104:29–30: he sustains and renews what lives.
- Acts 17:25: he needs nothing and gives everything.
- John 11:25: Jesus is the resurrection and the life.
- Rom 8:11: he raises the dead by his Spirit.
- Rev 21:5: he makes all things new.
God is always the giver. He creates what is good, sustains every breath, raises the dead and renews his creation.

- Ps 113:5–8: enthroned on high, he stoops down and raises the poor.
- Isa 40:11; 57:15: he gently leads his flock and dwells with the lowly and contrite.
- Matt 11:29; 21:5: Jesus is gentle and humble in heart, a king on a donkey.
- Mark 10:45; John 13:3–5, 14: he came to serve and washes his disciples' feet.
- Phil 2:6–8: he humbled himself, even to death on a cross.
- Gal 5:22–23: the Spirit brings forth gentleness.

The Most High does not hold himself at a distance from the lowly. He stoops, serves and deals gently with the weak. This is seen most clearly in Jesus, and the Spirit forms the same gentleness in people.
